questions.stem: What are the three components of a DNA nucleotide?

options.text: Phosphate group, deoxyribose sugar, and a nitrogenous base

questions.explanation: Each DNA nucleotide consists of three parts: a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar (a 5-carbon sugar), and one of four nitrogenous bases (adenine, thymine, guanine, or cytosine). The sugar-phosphate groups form the backbone, while the bases carry the genetic information.

questions.stem: Why are natural polymers generally biodegradable while synthetic addition polymers are not?

options.text: Natural polymers contain hydrolysable links that enzymes can break down, while addition polymers have only strong C-C bonds
Synthetic polymers are made from carbon, which cannot be broken down
Natural polymers dissolve in water but synthetic ones do not

questions.explanation: Natural polymers contain ester or amide links that microorganisms have evolved enzymes to hydrolyse. Synthetic addition polymers have only strong, non-polar C-C bonds with no functional groups for enzymes to attack. No natural enzymes exist to break them down, so they persist in the environment.
